headline: Enchantments Lottery and Peak Season Lodging Checks
reservation: Overnight camping in the Enchantments zones requires a highly competitive lottery permit from May through October; day hiking is currently permitted with a self-issue pass at trailheads. The village itself experiences extreme demand during Oktoberfest and the December Christmas Lighting; lodging should be booked six to twelve months in advance. Always verify the latest permit boundaries and quotas via the Forest Service before travel.

days.title: Bavarian Village and River Vistas

stops.name: Waterfront Park
stops.detail: Walk the gentle trails along the Wenatchee River to spot local birdlife and enjoy views of the surrounding peaks.

stops.name: Leavenworth Nutcracker Museum
stops.detail: Explore a unique collection of thousands of nutcrackers from around the world in the heart of the village.

days.driving: Minimal; allow 15 minutes for local parking; conditions vary by festival season
days.note: Village parking fills very early during October weekends and the December holiday season.

days.title: Alpine Lakes and High Cascades

stops.name: Colchuck Lake Trailhead
stops.detail: Begin a strenuous trek toward the turquoise waters of Colchuck Lake, set against the backdrop of Dragontail Peak.

stops.name: Icicle Ridge Trail
stops.detail: Ascend for panoramic views overlooking the Leavenworth valley and the rugged Wenatchee Mountains.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes for Forest Service roads; conditions vary with snow and washouts
days.note: High elevation trails often remain snow-covered until July; check seasonal melt status.

days.title: Glacial Lakes and Canyons

stops.name: Lake Wenatchee State Park
stops.detail: Visit this large glacier-fed lake for kayaking or beach relaxation with views of the North Cascades.

stops.name: Tumwater Canyon
stops.detail: Stop at various pull-offs to witness the powerful Wenatchee River rapids and dramatic granite canyon walls.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour total driving; check WSDOT for Highway 2 pass conditions
days.note: Afternoon winds at Lake Wenatchee can be strong; water temperatures remain cool year-round.

intel.title: Downtown Congestion
intel.text: Parking in the Bavarian village core is limited and highly competitive during festival weekends. Consider using peripheral lots or local shuttles if available during peak events.

intel.title: Canyon Dead Zones
intel.text: Cellular reception is generally reliable in town but drops significantly once entering Tumwater Canyon or Icicle Road. Download offline maps before leaving the village center.

intel.title: Village Services
intel.text: Leavenworth offers full services, but fuel stations are sparse once you head deep into the Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest. Ensure your tank is full before beginning long mountain drives.

intel.title: Mid-Week Advantage
intel.text: To avoid the largest crowds and high accommodation rates, plan your visit for Monday through Thursday. This is especially relevant during the autumn leaf-peeping season and winter holidays.

intel.title: Forest Road Status
intel.text: Access to high-elevation trailheads like Stuart Lake depends on seasonal snow removal and road maintenance. Check the official Forest Service road status page for closures due to winter weather or washouts.

plan.arrival: Pick up your vehicle at Pangborn Memorial (EAT) or Seattle-Tacoma (SEA). Stop in Wenatchee or downtown Leavenworth for mountain supplies and Northwest Forest Passes before heading to trailheads.
plan.vehicle: A standard car is sufficient for town and major highways, but high-clearance vehicles are recommended for unpaved Forest Service roads. Check rental agreements for restrictions on unpaved surfaces.
plan.goldenHour: Icicle Ridge is a substantial hike, not a roadside sunset stop: the initial viewpoint outing is about 6 miles round trip. Prefer a daylight return and allow enough time for the descent.
